mainTopic: Rules for writing and placing a מזוזה and תפילין (surface, שרטוט, writing by heart, placement), plus honoring a ספר תורה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: תפילין that were 'changed' are פסול when written on the wrong side, such as on דוכסוסטוס on the flesh side. A second answer says the ruling that a change is פסול is disputed among תנאים. The גמרא then asks how worn תפילין could ever become a מזוזה, since a מזוזה needs שרטוט, and answers that רבי ירמיה holds neither one needs it. The final הלכה is that a מזוזה needs שרטוט, תפילין do not, and both may be written by heart. Next comes a report that רב הונא would not sit on a bed with a ספר תורה on it, while רבי יוחנן permits it and explains away a story about רבי אלעזר. The amud returns to מזוזה: one written casually like a letter is פסולה, one hung on a stick is פסולה because it must be 'upon your gates', and the household of King מונבז did this only as a reminder. Finally, שמואל says the מזוזה belongs inside the doorway's opening, and the גמרא begins explaining why that is not obvious; the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the answer: תפילין written on the flesh side of דוכסוסטוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer. 'Changed in this way or that way' refers to תפילין written on the wrong side, for example on דוכסוסטוס on the side that faced the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he wrote them on דוכסוסטוס, on the side that faced the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing an answer that began just before this section. It explains that the case of a forbidden 'change' is about תפילין written on the wrong side of the hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal hide can be split into two layers. The outer layer is קלף and the inner layer is דוכסוסטוס, and each one has its own correct writing side. Writing תפילין on דוכסוסטוס on the flesh side is the wrong side, so such תפילין are פסול. This answer leaves room to say that a מזוזה written on קלף is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner layer of a split animal hide, used for writing
On the side of the hide that faced the animal's flesh
The outer layer of a split hide, the one that faced the hair

phrases.english: where he wrote them on dukhsustos, on the side of the flesh.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the תפילין. This finishes a sentence that started just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun before this section, which explains which 'change' makes something פסול
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'change' is about תפילין, not a מזוזה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that a מזוזה written on קלף is פסול
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling of פסול is about תפילין written on the wrong side, such as on דוכסוסטוס on the flesh side, so a מזוזה on קלף can still be כשר

steps.title: Second answer: תנאים argue about changing the writing surface
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the ruling that changing makes it פסול may really be about a מזוזה on קלף. This is simply one side of a disagreement among תנאים, since another תנא holds it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you wish, say that 'changed in this way or that way' is a disagreement among תנאים. A ברייתא teaches that if he changed in this way or that way, it is פסול. רבי אחא rules it כשר in the name of רבי אחאי son of רבי חנינא, and some say in the name of רבי עקיבא son of רבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way out. It admits the ruling may be about a מזוזה on קלף, but says other תנאים disagree with that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer changed what the case is about. This answer keeps the simple reading and instead shows that the ruling is disputed. So the opinion that a מזוזה on קלף is כשר has support from רבי אחא, who rules a change is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say': introduces a second, different answer
It is a disagreement among תנאים
He changed, meaning he wrote on a surface or side other than the usual one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rejection of the first answer. It is a second, separate way to solve the same problem, and both answers stand side by side.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
'he changed in this or in that' is a dispute of tanna'im,
as it is taught: if he changed in this or in that, it is unfit;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי [אַחָא מַכְשִׁיר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי] אַחַאי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha deems it fit in the name of Rabbi Achai son of Rabbi Chanina,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets belong to the corrected wording, so read it as 'רבי אחא rules it כשר in the name of רבי אחאי.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: and some say it in the name of Rabbi Akiva son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: שִׁינָּה בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same problem that Step 1 answered
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the ruling is disputed among תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling 'changed, it is פסול' seemed to be agreed by everyone and to cover a מזוזה on קלף
steps.terutzMaskana: That ruling is only one opinion. רבי אחא rules such a change כשר, so the opinion allowing a מזוזה on קלף has a תנא to rely on.

steps.title: Challenge: a מזוזה needs שרטוט, so how could תפילין become one?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא implies that worn תפילין could be made into a מזוזה if not for the rule against lowering holiness. The גמרא objects that a מזוזה needs שרטוט, which is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא implies that if we were allowed to lower holiness, we could make a מזוזה from them. But a מזוזה needs שרטוט! רב מניומי בר חלקיה said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא in the name of רב: any מזוזה that is not scored is פסול. And רב מנימין בר חלקיה himself said: the שרטוט of a מזוזה is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the ברייתא about worn תפילין and raises a problem. A מזוזה needs scored lines, so תפילין parchment could never become a מזוזה anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only one reason against making a מזוזה from תפילין: we do not lower holiness. That suggests that without this reason it would work. But a מזוזה requires שרטוט by הלכה למשה מסיני, and no such rule is taught for תפילין, so the parchment would be missing something a מזוזה needs. The ברייתא should then have given that simpler reason.

keyTerms.meaning: We lower, meaning we move an item from greater holiness to lesser holiness
Scoring, meaning lines etched into the parchment before writing
A law given orally to משה at סיני, not learned from a פסוק

phrases.english: This implies that if we lower holiness, we may make them,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא saying worn תפילין can't become a מזוזה because we don't lower holiness.

phrases.english: but a mezuza requires scoring!
As Rav Minyomei bar Chilkiya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
Any mezuza that is not scored is unfit;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב מִנְיָמִין בַּר חִלְקִיָּה דִּידֵיהּ אָמַר:
phrases.english: and Rav Minyamin bar Chilkiya himself said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׂרְטוּט שֶׁל מְזוּזָה הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי.
phrases.english: the scoring of a mezuza is a halakha to Moshe from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מוֹרִידִין עוֹשִׂין וְהָא בָּעֲיָא שִׂרְטוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of questioning on the ברייתא about worn תפילין
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the ברייתא that, if lowering holiness were allowed, worn תפילין could be made into a מזוזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מזוזה needs שרטוט by הלכה למשה מסיני, and nothing says תפילין need it. So תפילין parchment could not become a מזוזה even if lowering holiness were allowed, and the ברייתא should have given that reason instead.

steps.title: Answer: a תנא holds neither תפילין nor מזוזות need שרטוט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the need for שרטוט is a disagreement among תנאים. The ברייתא follows רבי ירמיה in the name of רב, who says תפילין and מזוזות may be written without copying from a text and need no שרטוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a disagreement among תנאים. A ברייתא teaches that רבי ירמיה says in the name of our teacher: תפילין and מזוזות may be written without copying from a written text, and they do not need שרטוט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that not everyone requires שרטוט for a מזוזה. The ברייתא about worn תפילין follows the view that no שרטוט is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ירמיה, neither a מזוזה nor תפילין need scored lines. So under that view, the only thing stopping us from turning worn תפילין into a מזוזה is the rule against lowering holiness, just as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Not from a written text, meaning the scribe writes without copying from a written copy in front of him
'Our teacher'; here it refers to רב

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on whether a מזוזה needs שרטוט. רב rules that an unscored מזוזה is פסולה, and רב מנימין בר חלקיה adds that שרטוט is a הלכה למשה מסיני. רבי ירמיה, in the name of רבינו, holds that neither תפילין nor מזוזות need it. The ברייתא about worn תפילין fits the second view.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yirmeya says in the name of our teacher:

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִילִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת נִכְתָּבוֹת שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַכְּתָב,
phrases.english: Tefillin and mezuzot may be written not from a written text,
and they do not require scoring.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the requirement is disputed among תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees a מזוזה needs שרטוט, so תפילין could never become a מזוזה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי ירמיה, who holds that neither תפילין nor מזוזות need שרטוט, so only the rule against lowering holiness stands in the way

steps.title: The final ruling on scoring lines and writing by heart
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that תפילין do not need שרטוט, a מזוזה does need שרטוט, and both may be written without copying from a text, because scribes know them well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The final ruling: תפילין don't need scored lines, but a מזוזה does. Both may be written by heart, not copied from a text. Why? Because these passages are so familiar.
steps.whatsHappening: After the debate about whether a מזוזה needs שרטוט, the גמרא gives the practical ruling. It also explains why writing them by heart is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי ירמיה in the name of רב grouped תפילין and מזוזות together, saying both may skip שרטוט. The final הלכה splits them: only תפילין may skip שרטוט, while a מזוזה needs it. On writing by heart they stay the same, because scribes know these short passages very well.

keyTerms.meaning: They are well known and fluent in everyone's mouth
These and those, meaning both of them

steps.whatToRemember: תפילין: no שרטוט needed. מזוזה: שרטוט needed. Both may be written by heart because the texts are so familiar.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rules. On שרטוט, תפילין and מזוזה are different. On writing by heart, they are the same.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling that scribes follow when writing תפילין and מזוזות.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: tefillin do not require scoring,
but a mezuza requires scoring,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי נִכְתָּבוֹת שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַכְּתָב.
phrases.english: and both these and those may be written not from a written text.
What is the reason? They are well known.
phrases.notes: Literally 'they are well studied.' Scribes know these short passages by heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the practical הלכה after the debate among תנאים about שרטוט in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תפילין need no שרטוט, a מזוזה needs שרטוט, and both may be written by heart because they are well known.

steps.title: רב הונא would not sit on a bed with a ספר תורה on it
steps.stepSummary: רב חלבו saw רב הונא move a ספר תורה off a bed onto an upside-down jug before sitting on the bed. This shows he held that sitting on such a bed is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חלבו said: I saw רב הונא when he wanted to sit on a bed that had a ספר תורה on it. He turned a jug upside down on the floor, put the ספר תורה on it, and only then sat on the bed. He held that it is forbidden to sit on a bed while a ספר תורה is lying on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, the honor of a ספר תורה. It brings an eyewitness report of how רב הונא acted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא did not want to sit on the same bed as the ספר תורה, because that would treat it disrespectfully. He also did not put it straight on the floor. He raised it onto an overturned jug first. From his actions the גמרא learns his ruling: sitting on such a bed is אסור.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥelbo said:
I saw Rav Huna
as he was going to sit on a bed
that had a Torah scroll on it,
and he turned a jug over on the ground,
and placed the Torah scroll on it,
and then sat on the bed.
He holds: it is forbidden to sit

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי מִיטָּה שֶׁסֵּפֶר תּוֹרָה מוּנָּח עָלֶיהָ.
phrases.english: on a bed upon which a Torah scroll is placed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֶלְבּוֹ: אֲנָא חֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about honoring a ספר תורה, brought here because it is another report from רב חלבו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב הונא, it is forbidden to sit on a bed while a ספר תורה is lying on it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן permits sitting on such a bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב הונא's view disagrees with רבי יוחנן, who rules that sitting on a bed with a ספר תורה on it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבה בר בר חנה, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is permitted to sit on a bed that has a ספר תורה on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another sage, רבי יוחנן, disagrees with רב הונא. It quotes his ruling that sitting on such a bed is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two opposite opinions about the same case. רב הונא says it is אסור, and רבי יוחנן says it is מותר. The next lines bring a story that seems to go against רבי יוחנן, and then answer it.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabba bar bar Ḥana,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is permitted to sit on a bed
upon which a Torah scroll is placed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opinion that disagrees with רב הונא's ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, it is permitted to sit on a bed with a ספר תורה on it.

steps.title: A story that seems to go against רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's statement continues by raising a possible challenge: רבי אלעזר jumped off a bed in alarm when he realized a ספר תורה was there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone whispers to you: There was a story with רבי אלעזר, who was sitting on a bed and remembered that a ספר תורה was lying there. He slipped off and sat on the ground, looking like someone bitten by a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside his own statement, רבי יוחנן brings up a story someone might use against his ruling. He is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר leaped off the bed in alarm. That makes it look like sitting on a bed with a ספר תורה is seriously wrong. If so, רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Whispers to you, quietly suggests to you

phrases.english: And if a person whispers to you, saying:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב עַל הַמִּיטָּה
phrases.english: There was an incident with Rabbi Elazar, who was sitting on the bed
and remembered that a Torah scroll was placed on it,
and he slipped off and sat on the ground,
and he looked like one whom a snake had bitten,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible challenge to רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that sitting on a bed with a ספר תורה on it is מותר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר's alarmed reaction suggests that sitting on such a bed is forbidden.

steps.title: In that story the ספר תורה was on the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that in רבי אלעזר's story the ספר תורה was on the ground, not on the bed, so the story proves nothing about his case.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the ספר תורה was on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the story by showing it was a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אלעזר's case, the ספר תורה was lying on the ground while he sat above it on the bed. That is clearly disrespectful, so his alarm makes sense. It says nothing about a ספר תורה lying on the same bed, which רבי יוחנן permits.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא forbids sitting on a bed with a ספר תורה on it. רבי יוחנן permits it. Everyone agrees you may not sit on a bed while the ספר תורה is lower, on the ground.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע הֲוָה.
phrases.english: There, the Torah scroll was on the ground.
phrases.notes: Read the story this way: רבי אלעזר realized the ספר תורה was lying below him on the ground, and that is why he jumped down.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי אלעזר's story in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (the story involved a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's reaction shows that sitting on a bed with a ספר תורה on it is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: In that story the ספר תורה was on the ground, below him, which is truly disrespectful. When it is on the bed itself, sitting there is מותר.

steps.title: A מזוזה written casually like a letter is invalid
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a מזוזה written like a casual letter is פסול. This is learned by comparing the word 'writing' used for מזוזה with the word 'writing' used for a ספר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone wrote a מזוזה like a letter, it is פסול. Why? We learn it from the word 'writing' in both places, comparing it to a ספר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the laws of writing a מזוזה. It brings שמואל's rule and his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A letter is written casually, without exact care for each letter. The תורה uses the word 'writing' for a מזוזה and also for a ספר, which must be written exactly. Because the same word appears in both places, the strict rules of a ספר carry over to a מזוזה, so a casual, letter-style מזוזה is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter, written casually without exactness
'Writing' and 'writing,' a comparison based on the same word (גזירה שוה)
It is learned from, it comes from
A scroll, which must be written precisely

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If one wrote it as a letter, it is unfit.
What is the reason?
It is derived from 'writing' and 'writing,' from a scroll.
phrases.notes: The word 'writing' appears for a מזוזה and also for a ספר, so the exact rules of a ספר apply to a מזוזה too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּתָבָהּ אִגֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of honoring a ספר תורה and goes back to the laws of writing a מזוזה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה written casually like a letter is פסול. This is learned by a גזירה שוה ('writing'/'writing') from a ספר.

steps.title: A מזוזה hung on a stick is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if someone hung a מזוזה on a stick instead of attaching it to the doorpost, it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone hung a מזוזה on a stick, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל about where a מזוזה must be. Hanging it from a stick in the doorway does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 was about how the מזוזה is written. Now שמואל moves to how it is placed. The מזוזה has to be fixed onto the doorway itself; just hanging it there is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The parchment with the פרשיות of שמע placed on the doorpost

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If one hung it on a stick, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּלָאָהּ בְּמַקֵּל – פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling from רב יהודה in the name of שמואל about מזוזה, now about placement instead of writing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה hung on a stick is פסולה.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a מזוזה on a stick is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind שמואל's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on שמואל. It is a request to know which פסוק or logic his ruling is based on.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a מזוזה hung on a stick is פסולה.

steps.title: The verse requires it to be on the gates
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'upon your gates,' so the מזוזה must be on the doorway itself, not hanging from a stick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק requires the מזוזה to be on the gate or doorway. A stick is not the gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ means 'upon your gates.' A מזוזה hanging from a stick is in the doorway but not on it, so the פסוק's requirement is not met.

keyTerms.meaning: Upon your gates (from the פסוק about מזוזה)

phrases.english: We require "upon your gates."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says 'upon your gates,' so the מזוזה must be attached to the doorway itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this ruling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: a מזוזה on a stick, or one placed behind the door, is a danger and fulfills no מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: If someone hung a מזוזה on a stick, or put it behind the door, it is a danger and there is no מצוה in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with שמואל. It also adds a second bad case: putting the מזוזה behind the door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms the stick ruling. It adds that placing it behind the door is also wrong, and that doing these things is not only useless for the מצוה but also a סכנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a source that supports the ruling)
There is no מצוה fulfilled through it

steps.whatToRemember: A מזוזה must be attached to the doorway itself. Hanging it on a stick or putting it behind the door does not fulfill the מצוה.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
If one hung it on a stick,
or placed it behind the door,
it is a danger, and there is no מצוה in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's ruling from step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a מזוזה on a stick is פסולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that a מזוזה on a stick or behind the door is a danger and fulfills no מצוה.

steps.title: King מונבז's household hung מזוזות on sticks as a reminder
steps.stepSummary: The household of King מונבז hung מזוזות on sticks in the inns where they stayed, only as a reminder of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The household of King מונבז used to do this in their inns, as a reminder of the מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. The family of King מונבז hung מזוזות on sticks when staying in inns, not to fulfill the מצוה but to remember it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After saying a מזוזה on a stick is פסולה, the גמרא shows that there was still a use for it. The family knew it was not a real מצוה, so they called it a זכר, a reminder.
steps.confusionAlert: This story does not mean a מזוזה on a stick is kosher. The גמרא says it was only a זכר, a reminder, not the real מצוה.

phrases.english: Those of the household of King Munbaz
would do so in their inns,
as a remembrance of the mezuza.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל בֵּית מוֹנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בְּפוּנְדְּקוֹתֵיהֶן כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells of a practice of hanging a מזוזה on a stick, while making clear it was only a reminder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hanging a מזוזה on a stick can serve as a reminder, but it is not the מצוה.

steps.title: The מזוזה belongs inside the opening of the doorway
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the מצוה is to place the מזוזה within the space of the doorway's opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The מצוה is to place it inside the opening of the doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives another rule about placement. The מזוזה should be inside the space of the doorway, not on the outside of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 taught that the מזוזה must be on the doorway. This step adds where on the doorway: inside the opening itself, in the space between the doorposts.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to place it
The inner space of the doorway's opening

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is a מצוה to place it
within the airspace of the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מִצְוָה לְהַנִּיחָהּ בְּתוֹךְ חֲלָלוֹ שֶׁל פֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further placement ruling from the same chain, רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזוזה should be placed inside the opening of the doorway.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious from the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל needs to say this, since the פסוק already says 'upon your gates.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! The Torah says 'upon your gates'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling as unnecessary. If the פסוק says the מזוזה goes on the gates, of course it belongs in the doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not that שמואל is wrong. It is that his statement seems to teach nothing new, because the פסוק already makes it clear.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: It is obvious!
The Merciful One said "upon your gates"!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the מזוזה goes inside the opening of the doorway.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'upon your gates' already teaches this, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Beginning the answer: we might have thought otherwise because of רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain that someone might have thought differently, based on a statement of רבא about where to place the מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that, since רבא said: It is a מצוה to place it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to why שמואל's rule is needed. It brings a statement of רבא that could have led to a different idea; the answer continues after this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פשיטא challenge is usually answered by showing a reasonable mistake someone could have made. Here the possible mistake comes from רבא's rule about placing the מזוזה, which is cut off here and finished in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say (a possible wrong idea)

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say,
since Rava said:
It is a מצוה to place it

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא, הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the פשיטא challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the ruling is needed to block a possible mistake (סלקא דעתך).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of רבא's statement about placing the מזוזה, one might have placed it somewhere other than inside the doorway's opening.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full answer continues after this point.
